records.title: Scotland Against Spin
records.bodyText:
The South Planning Applications Committee (SPAC) of the Highland Council will consider the Glen Earrach Energy (GEE) application at their meeting next Wednesday (7th Oct).
This may surprise some of you, as we are still in an active consultation period, following the 4th submission of further information by GEE. in September.  
For those you who don't read the Environmental Impact Assessment (Scotland) Regulations 2017, at bedtime - the consultation period for additional or supplementary information for an EIA is a minimum of 30 days. The consultation period remains open until the 5th Oct (next Monday).
Sound planning practice should mean that the Officer would wait until the end of that consultation period and ensure all relevant information is reviewed before completing the report on an application of this nature.
The Highland Council have opted to arbitrarily truncate the statutory minimum consultation period and the Officers report was issued a week prior to consultation deadline.
Clearly the Highland Council don't wish to consider any more responses and/or they are under pressure to get the application to committee.
This has potential ramifications for the outcome of the SPAC meeting, as matters of 'material consideration' may be overlooked!
The decision to unilaterally stop the consultation clock prior to the published deadline could prejudice any decision made next week.
BBC.CO.UK Glen Earrach Pumped Storage Hydro scheme to go before councillors

Viva la France!
Off the back of the UK.
Why do our politicians, including super-socialists like Burnham, think it okay to sell us out over and over and over again? Is the UK - is SCOTLAND - so weak and pathetic that we must continue to trod down the muddy path we are on, with regards to energy?
There are so many to blame for the mess we are in, and so many massive changes need to be made to get us out of it. But the road we are currently on is socially unethical, so environmentally destructive, so economically unfeasible, and will truly bring about the end of this nation. All empires crumble from within!
But then what????????????????????????????????????????
This is what the CEO of EDF thinks of the whole shebang in the UK...
"Simone Rossi is the CEO of EDF UK. He is on the BBC Radio 4 Today programme this morning explaining why UK energy bills will need to increase by 16%. His suggestion is that the UK needs to abandon its climate policies and open up fossil fuel resources
Mr Rossi’s UK company made £3.9 billion in profit in 2023, £2.9 billion in 2024, and £1.9 billion in 2025. His company is on course to make £1.7 billion this year. Mr Rossi pays himself £1 million a year, more than twice the salary of the head of his own global company, based in France, where the salary is capped by law. This is because EDF is a fully nationalised energy company in France. Using a deliberately crude piece of maths, Mr Rossi’s company makes a profit of about £850 a year out of each of its customers - mostly driven by the generation, rather than supply, side of the company.
Remarkably, no one at the BBC thought to make the suggestion that a very simple way to keep prices low for consumers, an opportunity which doesn’t require us to set fire to the planet, would be to stop Mr Rossi’s company excessively profiteering from energy. And perhaps reduce executive salaries at EDF UK to their own established global standards. You know, like they do in France."

PLANS have been submitted for an immense data centre campus in Dumfries and Galloway which, if built, would be the largest in the world. The proposals, submitted to Dumfries and Galloway Council yesterday on behalf of CX Tech Limited, include plans for eight 120MW data centres on land north of the decommissioned nuclear power station at Chapelcross.
However, campaigners have expressed concerns over the plans, particularly as they were submitted just weeks after the Scottish Government agreed to pause decisions on applications for hyperscale data centres until national guidance is produced. They estimate that the centre will require seven million MWh [megawatt-hours] of energy per year, although developers state the centres will be “designed to be operationally net zero”.
“This will put the Scottish Government on the spot – they have said that developers can still put in applications, but also agreed that no decisions will be taken until guidance is in place. They need to immediately make much clearer their position to local authorities and to the developers.
“It is for just these kinds of situations that we need guidance. We can’t have developments landing in Scotland that would use in a year the equivalent of a third of Scotland’s
THENATIONAL.SCOT Plans submitted for 'largest data centre campus in the world' in Scotland

Andy Burnham’s announcement of a new Great British Grid puts an important issue firmly on the national agenda: Britain needs a smarter, more strategic approach to electricity infrastructure.
The key question is not whether we need clean energy - we absolutely do. It is how we connect that energy in a way that delivers value for consumers while protecting communities, landscapes and our natural environment.
SEAS has consistently argued for a more integrated approach, including offshore grid connections and greater use of existing infrastructure and brownfield locations where appropriate.
A genuinely strategic Great British Grid could provide an opportunity to look beyond individual projects and consider the network as a whole — reducing unnecessary infrastructure, improving resilience and ensuring that investment delivers maximum benefit.
We welcome the focus on better coordination, faster connections and value for consumers.

Building a major wind farm near two air bases could invite "sabotage" from hostile nations, an MP has warned.
Nick Timothy, the Conservative MP for West Suffolk, questioned the suitability of building Redmere Wind Farm near the key US Air Force (USAF) bases of RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall, which are in his constituency.
"I have warned repeatedly that battery energy storage systems near important airbases is an invitation for hostile states and others to commit acts of sabotage," Timothy said.

records.title: Scotland Against Spin
records.bodyText:
Rural residents close to a proposed wind farm in Caithness will face “unacceptable” levels of shadow flicker if the development goes ahead . Campaign group Scotland Against Spin says shadow flicker – a visual effect caused when rotating turbines cut through sunlight – should not exceed 30 hours a year.
However, research carried out by a retired engineer who lives near the Olrig Mains Wind Farm site indicates that some properties could experience over 100 hours of the phenomenon and, “in the worst case”, over 180 hours.
Renewable energy company Green Switch Capital announced this month that it was lowering the maximum tip height of the four turbines from 200m to 180m following environmental assessments and feedback from the community.
It insists the Olrig scheme “has been designed to minimise potential effects of shadow flicker through careful turbine placement”.
Scotland Against Spin spokesperson Aileen Jackson, who lives in East Renfrewshire, said: “The standard planning benchmark used across the UK is that shadow flicker from wind turbines at neighbouring dwellings should not exceed 30 minutes per day or 30 hours per year, so this level of flicker is unacceptable.
“While the general rule of thumb suggests shadow flicker is only an issue within 10 rotor diameters of a turbine, evidence proves this is inadequate. Scotland Against Spin has received numerous complaints over the years of flicker well beyond this threshold.
“Personally, I have experienced severe flicker from turbines with a 90m rotor diameter at a distance of 1 km.
“We were advised by environmental health to make videos and keep a diary for a year. This proved that it breached the 30 hours a year guidance and the operator agreed to apply a software fix to shut down the turbines any time flicker occurred, i.e. on clear winter days when the sun was low in the sky.
“But we were very fortunate as often environmental health officers are reluctant to intervene, and operators are unwilling to apply software fixes due to the financial impact of forced downtime.
“We also have problems with flicker at night caused by the blades passing in front of the turbine aviation lights. There is nothing that can be done about this and our environmental health officer told us it was not a statutory nuisance because the frequency was not fast enough to induce an epileptic fit. He advised us to buy blackout curtains!”
